summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a string.
description: `nonString(value)` is the same test as `!isString(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
The test is `typeof value === "string"`, so the empty string passes and a `String` object, being an object, does not.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a string; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonString(1); // => true
nonString(null); // => true
nonString([]); // => true
nonString(""); // => false
nonString("abc"); // => false
```
